newsitem.title: INDIA: India not raising oil prices now - minister.
newsitem.headline: India not raising oil prices now - minister.

text.p: Indian junior Petroleum Minister T.R. Balu reiterated on Tuesday that the government did not plan at this time to raise the prices of petroleum products to curb burgeoning oil subsidies.
"We are not raising oil prices now, but we will take care of the oil pool deficit," Balu told Reuters on the margins of an energy conference in the Indian capital.
Asked how the government would take care of the oil pool deficit, Balu said: "We will try to find out some ways. You people suggest what we can do."

Oil prices in India are controlled by the government. Drawing from the oil pool account, the government reimburses oil firms for the difference between what they pay to import crude and what domestic refiners pay them.
Petroleum Ministry officials estimate that the oil pool deficit is expected to touch 155 billion rupees in 1996/97 (April-March) against 57 billion rupees last year.

In recent weeks government officials have played down the prospect of a short-term rise in the prices of petroleum products, citing strong opposition from left-wing parties in Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's centre-left coalition.
